lessons.title: Preparing to receive seed
lessons.html:
Preparing to receive seed

Seed arrives at the processing plant or warehouse from contract growers, trial fields or other seed companies. Receiving is the first control point. If the wrong seed is accepted, mixed with another lot or not recorded, the problem follows the seed all the way to the farmer. In the harvest season, many trucks may arrive each day, so the receiving team must be well organised.

Before the truck arrives

  • Know which deliveries are expected: grower, crop, cultivar, field or contract number, and estimated quantity. This comes from the production plan or harvest schedule.
  • Prepare intake bins, bays or storage space for each cultivar, cleaned and labelled. Never put a different cultivar into a bin until it is fully cleaned.
  • Check that the weighbridge or scale has been checked and is working.
  • Have sampling tools ready: probes or spears for bulk seed, bag triers, sample bags and labels.
  • Have the moisture meter ready and checked.
  • Have receiving forms or the system ready.

Safety at intake

  • Trucks and forklifts move around the yard. Wear a reflective vest and stay in pedestrian areas.
  • Never climb on a truck load without fall protection and permission.
  • Intake pits and augers can trap and kill people. Keep guards and grids in place. Never step into a pit while seed is moving.
  • Grain dust can cause breathing problems and can explode. Wear a dust mask and keep the area clean.

lessons.title: Receiving and sampling the delivery
lessons.html:
Receiving and sampling the delivery

Documents

  1. Check the delivery note: grower name, contract or field number, crop, cultivar, number of bags or bulk load.
  2. Check that the delivery is expected and the field was approved, for example in field inspection for certification.
  3. Record the truck registration and driver's name.

Weighing

Weigh the truck full on the weighbridge, and empty after offloading. The difference is the net mass. For bagged seed, count bags and weigh as procedure requires. Record weights clearly.

Sampling

A representative sample is taken from each load to check quality.

  • For bulk loads, probe the load at several points and depths in a set pattern.
  • For bags, sample from a set number of bags, from different positions in the load.
  • Mix the sample, label it with the intake number, and send it for moisture and quality checks.

Intake checks

CheckWhy
MoistureWet seed must be dried quickly or it heats and loses germination
Visual purityWeed seed, other crops, trash
DamageCracked, broken, insect-damaged seed
SmellMusty smell means fungi
Off-colour seedMay show mixing with another cultivar

Accept or reject

Compare results with the receiving standards in the contract or company procedure. If a load is clearly off-standard, for example very wet, mouldy or a different cultivar, hold it and call the supervisor before offloading. Do not mix doubtful loads with good seed.

Record the reason for any hold or rejection on the receiving slip and tell the grower or driver clearly. The grower's payment and contract may depend on this decision, so it must be based on measured results, not on opinion.

lessons.title: Offloading, recording and storing
lessons.html:
Offloading, recording and storing

Offloading

  • Direct the truck to the correct intake point or bay for that cultivar and lot.
  • Check that the intake system (pit, elevator, conveyor) is clean and set to the right bin.
  • Handle seed gently. Big drops and fast augers crack seed.
  • Bags should be stacked on clean pallets, not on the floor.
  • Keep each grower's delivery and each cultivar separate.

Labelling and lot numbers

Give each delivery an intake number or lot number according to company procedure. Put the number on the bin, bay or pallet, on the sample and on all documents. This links the seed to the grower and field for traceability.

Records

RecordExample
Intake or lot numberUnique number
Grower, contract, fieldFrom delivery note
Crop and cultivarFrom delivery note
Net massFrom weighbridge
Moisture and quality resultsFrom intake checks
Storage locationBin or bay number
Date, time and receiverYour name

Give the driver a signed copy of the receiving slip. Capture the information in the stock system on the same day. Growers are often paid on the receiving records, so they must be correct.

After intake

  • Send wet seed to the dryer as soon as possible.
  • Check temperature of stored seed regularly for heating.
  • Clean the intake pit and conveyors before the next cultivar.
  • Report any problems, such as damaged loads or differences in weight.

Key points

  • Know expected deliveries and prepare clean, labelled bins.
  • Check documents, weigh and take a representative sample.
  • Check moisture, purity, damage and smell before offloading.
  • Keep cultivars and growers separate with unique lot numbers.
  • Record accurately; growers are paid on receiving records.
